VOYAGE 1. Snow PROVIDENCE, Capt. H. Ainsley, from Kingston, Jamaica towards Bristol. Sailed Thursday 22 March 1781.

Thursday 22nd. Light airs from the N and rainy. People employed in stowing the boats. At noon lat. 39° 15' N, long. 43° 39' W. Saw a brig on the larboard bow. Served the people their allowance of beef and pork.

Friday 23rd. Light airs from the WNW and cloudy. People employed in stowing the boats. At noon lat. 39° 16' N, long. 44° 50' W. Saw a sail to windward standing to the eastward.

Saturday 24th. Variable winds from the W and thick fog. People employed in washing and scrubbing the decks. At noon lat. 38° 40' N, long. 45° 48' W. Saw a ship of war on the starboard tack. The pumps were worked an hour in every watch.

Sunday 25th. Gentle breezes from the NNW and a clear sky. People employed in scraping and tarring the standing rigging. At noon lat. 38° 40' N, long. 46° 50' W. Saw a ship of war on the starboard tack. Served the people their allowance of beef and pork.

Monday 26th. Fresh gales from the E and dark and gloomy. People employed in caulking the quarter-deck. At noon lat. 39° 5' N, long. 46° 47' W. Served bread and cheese to the people. Read the articles of war to the people.

Tuesday 27th. Little wind from the ESE and rainy. People employed in making points and gaskets. At noon lat. 39° 46' N, long. 47° 22' W. Saw a school of flying fish. Lost a handspike overboard.

Wednesday 28th. Strong gales from the SW and clear. People employed in washing and scrubbing the decks. At noon lat. 41° 11' N, long. 47° 49' W. Saw a large turtle asleep on the water.

Thursday 29th. Variable winds from the WNW and a clear sky. People employed in setting up the lower rigging. At noon lat. 40° 57' N, long. 48° 54' W. Served a pint of rum to each mess.

Friday 30th. Variable winds from the S and dark and gloomy. People employed in caulking the quarter-deck. At noon lat. 40° 23' N, long. 49° 35' W. Saw several porpoises about the ship.

Saturday 31st. Strong gales from the SSW and frequent showers. People employed in making points and gaskets. At noon lat. 39° 18' N, long. 50° 28' W. Served pease and oatmeal.

Sunday 1st April. Fresh gales from the NNE and squally. People employed in stowing the boats. At noon lat. 39° 19' N, long. 51° 29' W. Saw a large turtle asleep on the water.

Monday 2nd. Variable winds from the WSW and rainy. People employed in setting up the lower rigging. At noon lat. 39° 49' N, long. 52° 13' W. Read the articles of war to the people.

Tuesday 3rd. Light airs from the ENE and clear. People employed in setting up the lower rigging. At noon lat. 41° 6' N, long. 52° 23' W. Saw a school of flying fish. Served pease and oatmeal.

Wednesday 4th. Fresh gales from the SW and rainy. People employed in setting up the lower rigging. At noon lat. 40° 53' N, long. 52° 3' W. Opened a cask of beef, which proved sound. Read the articles of war to the people.

Thursday 5th. Variable winds from the WNW and thick fog. People employed in shifting the ballast. At noon lat. 40° 31' N, long. 52° 14' W. Saw a school of flying fish. Gave the people fresh fish for dinner. The long boat was washed from her chocks and recovered with some damage.

Friday 6th. Moderate gales from the NNW and thick fog. People employed in scraping and tarring the standing rigging. At noon lat. 39° 30' N, long. 52° 2' W. Served a pint of rum to each mess. The mate had a touch of the ague.

Saturday 7th. Strong gales from the WNW and squally. People employed in airing the bedding between decks. At noon lat. 39° 37' N, long. 53° 35' W.

Sunday 8th. Calms from the WNW and rainy. People employed in airing the bedding between decks. At noon lat. 40° 8' N, long. 53° 58' W. Served the people their allowance of beef and pork.

Monday 9th. Steady trades from the SSE and hazy. People employed in mending the main topsail. At noon lat. 41° 4' N, long. 53° 47' W. Served the people their allowance of beef and pork.

Tuesday 10th. Strong gales from the NE and clear. People employed in splicing the cable. At noon lat. 42° 39' N, long. 54° 38' W. Heard a noise in the hold and found a cask started; secured it.

Wednesday 11th. Moderate gales from the SSW and thick fog. People employed in working the pumps. At noon lat. 41° 48' N, long. 56° 19' W. Served bread and cheese to the people.

Thursday 12th. Variable winds from the NE and dark and gloomy. People employed in making points and gaskets. At noon lat. 43° 4' N, long. 56° 33' W. Served the people their allowance of beef and pork.

Friday 13th. Fresh breezes from the NE and thick fog. People employed in fishing the main yard. At noon lat. 44° 1' N, long. 56° 26' W. Saw a floating cask, much weathered. Mustered the people and found all well.

Saturday 14th. Little wind from the NNW and rainy. People employed in stowing the boats. At noon lat. 43° 57' N, long. 56° 55' W. Saw a floating cask, much weathered.

Sunday 15th. Gentle breezes from the SW and thick fog. People employed in setting up the lower rigging. At noon lat. 42° 50' N, long. 58° 0' W. Saw gulf weed in large patches. Gave the people fresh fish for dinner. Punished one of the boys for neglect of duty.

Monday 16th. Steady trades from the S and cloudy. People employed in setting up the lower rigging. At noon lat. 42° 40' N, long. 58° 45' W. Gave the people fresh fish for dinner. The mate had a touch of the ague.

Tuesday 17th. Light airs from the S and fair weather. People employed in splicing the cable. At noon lat. 43° 29' N, long. 60° 9' W. Served the people their allowance of beef and pork.

Wednesday 18th. Fresh breezes from the NE and thick fog. People employed in airing the bedding between decks. At noon lat. 42° 56' N, long. 61° 48' W. Saw a bird like a gannet. Served bread and cheese to the people. The mate had a touch of the ague.

Thursday 19th. Moderate gales from the NW and a clear sky. People employed in mending the main topsail. At noon lat. 42° 44' N, long. 62° 54' W. Saw the loom of land to the southward.

Friday 20th. Variable winds from the ESE and frequent showers. People employed in bending a new foresail. At noon lat. 44° 0' N, long. 64° 11' W. Saw several porpoises about the ship. Heard a noise in the hold and found a cask started; secured it.

Saturday 21st. Variable winds from the S and thick fog. People employed in shifting the ballast. At noon lat. 44° 1' N, long. 65° 16' W. Served a pint of rum to each mess.

Sunday 22nd. Moderate gales from the WNW and fair weather. People employed in setting up the lower rigging. At noon lat. 43° 18' N, long. 66° 27' W. The mate had a touch of the ague.

Monday 23rd. Fresh gales from the E and rainy. People employed in splicing the cable. At noon lat. 44° 0' N, long. 67° 4' W. Saw a brig on the larboard bow.

Tuesday 24th. Little wind from the NE and squally. People employed in splicing the cable. At noon lat. 44° 6' N, long. 67° 31' W. Saw the loom of land to the southward. The steward reported the water getting low and put the people on a short allowance.

Wednesday 25th. Moderate gales from the SSE and cloudy. People employed in mending the main topsail. At noon lat. 45° 0' N, long. 67° 50' W. Served bread and cheese to the people.

Thursday 26th. Strong gales from the NNW and rainy. People employed in fishing the main yard. At noon lat. 44° 40' N, long. 68° 52' W. Saw a whale blowing to leeward.

Friday 27th. Strong gales from the N and hazy. People employed in stowing the boats. At noon lat. 45° 2' N, long. 70° 41' W. Saw a bird like a gannet. Served the people their allowance of beef and pork.

Saturday 28th. Steady trades from the SW and squally. People employed in caulking the quarter-deck. At noon lat. 44° 1' N, long. 72° 31' W. Read the articles of war to the people.

Sunday 29th. Fresh breezes from the ESE and frequent showers. People employed in splicing the cable. At noon lat. 43° 31' N, long. 73° 44' W.

Monday 30th. Calms from the NNW and rainy. People employed in shifting the ballast. At noon lat. 42° 23' N, long. 74° 45' W.

Tuesday 1st May. Fresh gales from the S and hazy. People employed in bending a new foresail. At noon lat. 41° 34' N, long. 74° 30' W. Saw several porpoises about the ship.

Wednesday 2nd. Fresh breezes from the ESE and dark and gloomy. People employed in knotting yarns. At noon lat. 43° 4' N, long. 75° 40' W. Saw a floating cask, much weathered. Served a pint of rum to each mess.

Thursday 3rd. Calms from the SSW and clear. People employed in scraping and tarring the standing rigging. At noon lat. 41° 53' N, long. 77° 34' W. Saw a ship of war on the starboard tack.

Friday 4th. Fresh breezes from the WNW and hazy. People employed in making points and gaskets. At noon lat. 42° 7' N, long. 78° 22' W.

Sunday 6th. Light airs from the NNW and a clear sky. People employed in shifting the ballast. At noon lat. 41° 30' N, long. 80° 0' W. Saw a shoal of dolphins.

Monday 7th. Fresh breezes from the NW and frequent showers. People employed in caulking the quarter-deck. At noon lat. 42° 14' N, long. 80° 0' W. Saw a ship of war on the starboard tack. Served bread and cheese to the people. Lost a handspike overboard.

Sunday 13th. Steady trades from the NNW and rainy. People employed in knotting yarns. At noon lat. 42° 49' N, long. 79° 41' W. Gave the people fresh fish for dinner. Split the main topgallant sail in a squall; bent another.

VOYAGE 2. Ship HESTER, Capt. N. Pryce, from Bristol towards Cork. Sailed Monday 14 May 1781.

Monday 14th. Calms from the WNW and thick fog. People employed in caulking the quarter-deck. At noon lat. 34° 1' N, long. 29° 6' W.

Tuesday 15th. Fresh breezes from the W and rainy. People employed in stowing the boats. At noon lat. 35° 25' N, long. 30° 41' W. Served the people their allowance of beef and pork. The pumps were worked an hour in every watch.

Wednesday 16th. Fresh gales from the NNW and clear. People employed in fishing the main yard. At noon lat. 35° 11' N, long. 32° 18' W. Split the main topgallant sail in a squall; bent another.

Thursday 17th. Moderate gales from the WSW and cloudy. People employed in making points and gaskets. At noon lat. 35° 9' N, long. 32° 34' W. Saw gulf weed in large patches. Gave the people fresh fish for dinner. The mate had a touch of the ague.

Friday 18th. Moderate gales from the NW and squally. People employed in mending the main topsail. At noon lat. 36° 5' N, long. 33° 22' W. Saw a bird like a gannet. The mate had a touch of the ague.

Monday 21st. Calms from the N and dark and gloomy. People employed in setting up the lower rigging. At noon lat. 35° 37' N, long. 34° 19' W. Saw a bird like a gannet. Punished one of the boys for neglect of duty.

Friday 1st March. Fresh breezes from the N and dark and gloomy. People employed in splicing the cable. At noon lat. 39° 22' N, long. 31° 38' W. Served a pint of rum to each mess.

Saturday 2nd. Moderate gales from the ENE and clear. People employed in scraping and tarring the standing rigging. At noon lat. 39° 2' N, long. 33° 18' W.

VOYAGE 6. Snow PROVIDENCE, Capt. H. Ainsley, from Bristol towards Kingston, Jamaica. Sailed Saturday 27 April 1782.

Saturday 27th. Light airs from the S and cloudy. People employed in airing the bedding between decks. At noon lat. 44° 36' N, long. 30° 58' W. Saw a shoal of dolphins. The steward reported the water getting low and put the people on a short allowance.

Sunday 28th. Calms from the N and dark and gloomy. People employed in knotting yarns. At noon lat. 46° 8' N, long. 31° 55' W. Saw a whale blowing to leeward.

Monday 29th. Moderate gales from the E and dark and gloomy. People employed in working the pumps. At noon lat. 45° 58' N, long. 32° 40' W. Saw a large turtle asleep on the water.

Wednesday 1st May. Fresh breezes from the ENE and thick fog. People employed in knotting yarns. At noon lat. 46° 35' N, long. 32° 21' W. Saw a ship of war on the starboard tack. Opened a cask of beef, which proved sound.

Thursday 2nd. Steady trades from the E and clear. People employed in airing the bedding between decks. At noon lat. 46° 27' N, long. 33° 7' W. The cook scalded his arm and was laid up two days.

Friday 3rd. Light airs from the SW and dark and gloomy. People employed in caulking the quarter-deck. At noon lat. 46° 4' N, long. 32° 53' W. Read the articles of war to the people.

Wednesday 7th. Variable winds from the WNW and frequent showers. People employed in working the pumps. At noon lat. 12° 9' N, long. 24° 42' W. Saw gulf weed in large patches.

Friday 14th. Light airs from the SW and a clear sky. People employed in splicing the cable. At noon lat. 43° 0' N, long. 73° 23' W. Served bread and cheese to the people.

Sunday 16th. Calms from the SW and clear. People employed in knotting yarns. At noon lat. 42° 30' N, long. 75° 8' W.

Monday 17th. Variable winds from the SSE and a clear sky. People employed in airing the bedding between decks. At noon lat. 41° 57' N, long. 75° 5' W. Heard a noise in the hold and found a cask started; secured it.

Tuesday 18th. Light airs from the W and frequent showers. People employed in mending the main topsail. At noon lat. 42° 2' N, long. 76° 10' W. Served bread and cheese to the people.

Thursday 20th. Fresh breezes from the WSW and squally. People employed in airing the bedding between decks. At noon lat. 40° 14' N, long. 77° 0' W. Saw a whale blowing to leeward. Served a pint of rum to each mess.

Friday 21st. Fresh gales from the S and rainy. People employed in caulking the quarter-deck. At noon lat. 41° 47' N, long. 78° 34' W.

Wednesday 26th. Fresh breezes from the NNE and rainy. People employed in bending a new foresail. At noon lat. 41° 2' N, long. 80° 0' W. Saw a whale blowing to leeward. Samuel Moss, seaman, died after a short illness, and was buried with the usual ceremony.

Sunday 30th. Fresh breezes from the WNW and squally. People employed in stowing the boats. At noon lat. 13° 38' N, long. 42° 24' W. Saw a school of flying fish. Split the main topgallant sail in a squall; bent another.

Saturday 23rd. Little wind from the WSW and dark and gloomy. People employed in washing and scrubbing the decks. At noon lat. 29° 39' N, long. 36° 37' W. Served a pint of rum to each mess.

Sunday 24th. Steady trades from the NE and frequent showers. People employed in bending a new foresail. At noon lat. 30° 8' N, long. 37° 0' W. Saw a ship of war on the starboard tack. Heard a noise in the hold and found a cask started; secured it.

Monday 25th. Fresh gales from the NNE and fair weather. People employed in making points and gaskets. At noon lat. 29° 12' N, long. 36° 57' W.

Tuesday 26th. Gentle breezes from the SSE and frequent showers. People employed in shifting the ballast. At noon lat. 30° 14' N, long. 37° 3' W. Saw a shoal of dolphins. Served pease and oatmeal.

Wednesday 27th. Strong gales from the NNW and dark and gloomy. People employed in working the pumps. At noon lat. 29° 4' N, long. 37° 43' W. Saw several porpoises about the ship. The pumps were worked an hour in every watch.

Thursday 28th. Calms from the SSE and clear. People employed in stowing the boats. At noon lat. 30° 9' N, long. 38° 44' W. Saw Portuguese men-of-war in great numbers. Served the people their allowance of beef and pork. Lost a handspike overboard.

Friday 29th. Steady trades from the NE and squally. People employed in airing the bedding between decks. At noon lat. 31° 13' N, long. 39° 49' W. Opened a cask of pork, which was found rusty.

Saturday 30th. Moderate gales from the N and a clear sky. People employed in bending a new foresail. At noon lat. 32° 2' N, long. 41° 20' W. Served the people their allowance of beef and pork. Split the main topgallant sail in a squall; bent another.

Sunday 31st. Fresh gales from the NW and frequent showers. People employed in splicing the cable. At noon lat. 32° 44' N, long. 41° 27' W. Served bread and cheese to the people.

VOYAGE 20. Brig MARY ANN, Capt. E. Carew, from Bristol towards Cork. Sailed Tuesday 8 November 1785.

Tuesday 8th. Gentle breezes from the SSE and clear. People employed in shifting the ballast. At noon lat. 36° 5' N, long. 41° 36' W. Saw several porpoises about the ship. Served pease and oatmeal.

Wednesday 9th. Little wind from the SSW and clear. People employed in washing and scrubbing the decks. At noon lat. 36° 59' N, long. 42° 24' W. Saw a shoal of dolphins. Examined the casks and found three leaking.

Thursday 10th. Calms from the ENE and cloudy. People employed in setting up the lower rigging. At noon lat. 36° 14' N, long. 42° 36' W. Saw a large turtle asleep on the water. The steward reported the water getting low and put the people on a short allowance.

Wednesday 21st. Calms from the N and thick fog. People employed in making points and gaskets. At noon lat. 44° 50' N, long. 75° 52' W. Opened a cask of pork, which was found rusty. The mate had a touch of the ague.

VOYAGE 22. Ship HESTER, Capt. N. Pryce, from Bristol towards Lisbon. Sailed Tuesday 4 April 1786.

Tuesday 4th. Strong gales from the NE and frequent showers. People employed in splicing the cable. At noon lat. 37° 25' N, long. 9° 3' W. Saw several porpoises about the ship. The long boat was washed from her chocks and recovered with some damage.

Wednesday 5th. Moderate gales from the NNW and cloudy. People employed in airing the bedding between decks. At noon lat. 36° 16' N, long. 10° 36' W. Served bread and cheese to the people. Heard a noise in the hold and found a cask started; secured it.

VOYAGE 23. Brig MARY ANN, Capt. S. Kemp, from Lisbon towards Bristol. Sailed Wednesday 19 July 1786.

Wednesday 19th. Little wind from the NE and dark and gloomy. People employed in scraping and tarring the standing rigging. At noon lat. 43° 30' N, long. 12° 9' W. Opened a cask of beef, which proved sound.

Thursday 20th. Fresh breezes from the SE and rainy. People employed in mending the main topsail. At noon lat. 43° 16' N, long. 13° 41' W. Saw several porpoises about the ship. Served the people their allowance of beef and pork. Heard a noise in the hold and found a cask started; secured it.

Friday 21st. Light airs from the E and hazy. People employed in making points and gaskets. At noon lat. 43° 27' N, long. 15° 27' W. Saw Portuguese men-of-war in great numbers. Punished one of the boys for neglect of duty.

Saturday 22nd. Moderate gales from the SSW and clear. People employed in scraping and tarring the standing rigging. At noon lat. 43° 39' N, long. 15° 36' W. Saw a floating cask, much weathered. The steward reported the water getting low and put the people on a short allowance.

Sunday 23rd. Steady trades from the NNE and squally. People employed in knotting yarns. At noon lat. 44° 57' N, long. 15° 54' W. Saw gulf weed in large patches. Served a pint of rum to each mess.

Monday 24th. Fresh gales from the ESE and frequent showers. People employed in setting up the lower rigging. At noon lat. 45° 14' N, long. 16° 33' W. Saw a whale blowing to leeward. The pumps were worked an hour in every watch.

Tuesday 25th. Fresh breezes from the W and frequent showers. People employed in knotting yarns. At noon lat. 45° 5' N, long. 16° 24' W. Served pease and oatmeal. Heard a noise in the hold and found a cask started; secured it.

Thursday 27th. Gentle breezes from the S and thick fog. People employed in caulking the quarter-deck. At noon lat. 45° 43' N, long. 18° 28' W. Served pease and oatmeal. Punished one of the boys for neglect of duty.

VOYAGE 28. Brig MARY ANN, Capt. E. Carew, from Bristol towards Lisbon. Sailed Wednesday 19 September 1787.

Wednesday 19th. Strong gales from the WNW and a clear sky. People employed in working the pumps. At noon lat. 17° 5' N, long. 68° 25' W. Served bread and cheese to the people.

Thursday 20th. Moderate gales from the WNW and squally. People employed in fishing the main yard. At noon lat. 18° 36' N, long. 69° 30' W. Opened a cask of pork, which was found rusty.

Friday 21st. Gentle breezes from the NE and a clear sky. People employed in scraping and tarring the standing rigging. At noon lat. 19° 5' N, long. 70° 28' W. Served a pint of rum to each mess. The steward reported the water getting low and put the people on a short allowance.

Friday 22nd. Calms from the NE and a clear sky. People employed in scraping and tarring the standing rigging. At noon lat. 55° 0' N, long. 80° 0' W. Saw Portuguese men-of-war in great numbers. Gave the people fresh fish for dinner.

Saturday 23rd. Little wind from the WNW and fair weather. People employed in setting up the lower rigging. At noon lat. 54° 49' N, long. 80° 0' W. Opened a cask of pork, which was found rusty. Punished one of the boys for neglect of duty.

Sunday 24th. Fresh gales from the ESE and dark and gloomy. People employed in caulking the quarter-deck. At noon lat. 55° 0' N, long. 80° 0' W.

VOYAGE 37. Snow PROVIDENCE, Capt. J. Voss, from Kingston, Jamaica towards Bristol. Sailed Monday 19 April 1790.

Monday 19th. Steady trades from the W and cloudy. People employed in shifting the ballast. At noon lat. 12° 46' N, long. 10° 12' W.

Tuesday 20th. Strong gales from the SSW and clear. People employed in stowing the boats. At noon lat. 13° 25' N, long. 11° 31' W. Saw a whale blowing to leeward. The pumps were worked an hour in every watch.

Wednesday 21st. Gentle breezes from the SSE and clear. People employed in splicing the cable. At noon lat. 14° 42' N, long. 12° 48' W. Saw a brig on the larboard bow. Opened a cask of beef, which proved sound.

Thursday 22nd. Calms from the NNW and fair weather. People employed in shifting the ballast. At noon lat. 16° 14' N, long. 14° 25' W. Opened a cask of pork, which was found rusty.

Friday 23rd. Light airs from the SW and clear. People employed in washing and scrubbing the decks. At noon lat. 15° 54' N, long. 14° 40' W. Saw the loom of land to the southward. Served pease and oatmeal. The steward reported the water getting low and put the people on a short allowance.

Saturday 24th. Fresh gales from the SSE and fair weather. People employed in mending the main topsail. At noon lat. 16° 34' N, long. 14° 57' W. Served bread and cheese to the people. Split the main topgallant sail in a squall; bent another.

Sunday 25th. Moderate gales from the SSW and clear. People employed in splicing the cable. At noon lat. 16° 27' N, long. 14° 37' W. Served the people their allowance of beef and pork. Lost a handspike overboard.

Monday 26th. Fresh gales from the SW and hazy. People employed in stowing the boats. At noon lat. 16° 42' N, long. 15° 39' W. Saw a large turtle asleep on the water. Served the people their allowance of beef and pork. The long boat was washed from her chocks and recovered with some damage.

Tuesday 27th. Gentle breezes from the NE and cloudy. People employed in stowing the boats. At noon lat. 17° 11' N, long. 15° 39' W. Served the people their allowance of beef and pork. Split the main topgallant sail in a squall; bent another.

VOYAGE 41. Brig MARY ANN, Capt. S. Kemp, from Lisbon towards Bristol. Sailed Tuesday 22 March 1791.

Tuesday 22nd. Fresh breezes from the ESE and a clear sky. People employed in stowing the boats. At noon lat. 41° 48' N, long. 35° 35' W.

Monday 28th. Light airs from the NNE and squally. People employed in fishing the main yard. At noon lat. 44° 45' N, long. 41° 18' W. Saw a shoal of dolphins. Edward Cole, seaman, died of a fever, and was buried with the usual ceremony.

Tuesday 29th. Steady trades from the NE and dark and gloomy. People employed in fishing the main yard. At noon lat. 44° 57' N, long. 43° 11' W. Saw Portuguese men-of-war in great numbers. Served a pint of rum to each mess.

VOYAGE 53. Brig MARY ANN, Capt. E. Carew, from Lisbon towards Bristol. Sailed Tuesday 1 April 1794.

Tuesday 1st April. Moderate gales from the S and clear. People employed in knotting yarns. At noon lat. 30° 18' N, long. 45° 2' W. Saw a shoal of dolphins. Opened a cask of pork, which was found rusty. Heard a noise in the hold and found a cask started; secured it.

Friday 12th. Gentle breezes from the E and thick fog. People employed in washing and scrubbing the decks. At noon lat. 24° 17' N, long. 34° 54' W.

VOYAGE 61. Brig MARY ANN, Capt. S. Kemp, from Kingston, Jamaica towards Bristol. Sailed Thursday 11 August 1796.

Thursday 11th. Light airs from the NNE and dark and gloomy. People employed in stowing the boats. At noon lat. 48° 16' N, long. 32° 13' W. Saw Portuguese men-of-war in great numbers. Opened a cask of beef, which proved sound. The cook scalded his arm and was laid up two days.

VOYAGE 73. Brig MARY ANN, Capt. E. Carew, from Kingston, Jamaica towards Bristol. Sailed Friday 13 September 1799.

Friday 13th. Gentle breezes from the ENE and fair weather. People employed in making points and gaskets. At noon lat. 25° 39' N, long. 32° 13' W. Saw Portuguese men-of-war in great numbers. The pumps were worked an hour in every watch.

VOYAGE 82. Snow PROVIDENCE, Capt. J. Voss, from Bristol towards Lisbon. Sailed Sunday 21 February 1802.

Sunday 21st. Little wind from the NW and frequent showers. People employed in knotting yarns. At noon lat. 19° 25' N, long. 19° 31' W. Saw a large turtle asleep on the water.

Monday 22nd. Light airs from the WSW and rainy. People employed in bending a new foresail. At noon lat. 20° 28' N, long. 19° 7' W. Saw a bird like a gannet.

Tuesday 23rd. Steady trades from the NNW and hazy. People employed in working the pumps. At noon lat. 22° 0' N, long. 19° 33' W. Saw the loom of land to the southward. The long boat was washed from her chocks and recovered with some damage.

Wednesday 24th. Little wind from the NE and clear. People employed in washing and scrubbing the decks. At noon lat. 22° 33' N, long. 21° 20' W.

Thursday 18th. Calms from the WSW and fair weather. People employed in washing and scrubbing the decks. At noon lat. 32° 41' N, long. 47° 9' W. Served the people their allowance of beef and pork. Heard a noise in the hold and found a cask started; secured it.

Monday 3rd. Moderate gales from the WSW and thick fog. People employed in washing and scrubbing the decks. At noon lat. 37° 42' N, long. 55° 54' W. Saw a large turtle asleep on the water. The mate had a touch of the ague. Daniel Venn, seaman, died of the flux, and was buried with the usual ceremony.

Tuesday 4th. Strong gales from the N and fair weather. People employed in scraping and tarring the standing rigging. At noon lat. 37° 40' N, long. 55° 52' W. Saw a whale blowing to leeward. The steward reported the water getting low and put the people on a short allowance.

Wednesday 5th. Little wind from the E and frequent showers. People employed in washing and scrubbing the decks. At noon lat. 38° 51' N, long. 56° 44' W. Saw a brig on the larboard bow. Opened a cask of beef, which proved sound.

Thursday 6th. Moderate gales from the SSE and clear. People employed in fishing the main yard. At noon lat. 39° 47' N, long. 56° 23' W. The steward reported the water getting low and put the people on a short allowance.

Friday 7th. Little wind from the NNW and fair weather. People employed in fishing the main yard. At noon lat. 41° 13' N, long. 56° 39' W. Saw several porpoises about the ship.

Saturday 8th. Fresh gales from the NE and thick fog. People employed in working the pumps. At noon lat. 40° 41' N, long. 57° 50' W. Opened a cask of beef, which proved sound. The pumps were worked an hour in every watch.

Sunday 9th. Little wind from the SE and clear. People employed in knotting yarns. At noon lat. 41° 12' N, long. 58° 46' W. Gave the people fresh fish for dinner. Lost a handspike overboard.

Monday 10th. Light airs from the W and clear. People employed in overhauling the running rigging. At noon lat. 40° 19' N, long. 59° 33' W. Saw a bird like a gannet. Opened a cask of pork, which was found rusty. The long boat was washed from her chocks and recovered with some damage.

Tuesday 11th. Steady trades from the WSW and cloudy. People employed in stowing the boats. At noon lat. 40° 21' N, long. 60° 53' W. Saw the loom of land to the southward.

Wednesday 12th. Gentle breezes from the S and rainy. People employed in fishing the main yard. At noon lat. 41° 12' N, long. 61° 1' W. Saw several porpoises about the ship. Served bread and cheese to the people.

Thursday 13th. Strong gales from the E and thick fog. People employed in fishing the main yard. At noon lat. 41° 15' N, long. 61° 42' W. Saw a whale blowing to leeward.

Friday 14th. Steady trades from the ESE and dark and gloomy. People employed in airing the bedding between decks. At noon lat. 41° 23' N, long. 63° 16' W.

Saturday 15th. Variable winds from the E and thick fog. People employed in shifting the ballast. At noon lat. 41° 42' N, long. 64° 53' W. Served pease and oatmeal. The cook scalded his arm and was laid up two days.

Sunday 16th. Variable winds from the WSW and dark and gloomy. People employed in washing and scrubbing the decks. At noon lat. 41° 56' N, long. 66° 13' W. Saw a floating cask, much weathered. Opened a cask of pork, which was found rusty. The mate had a touch of the ague.

VOYAGE 94. Snow PROVIDENCE, Capt. H. Ainsley, from Bristol towards Lisbon. Sailed Wednesday 25 August 1802.

Wednesday 25th. Moderate gales from the NNE and hazy. People employed in washing and scrubbing the decks. At noon lat. 28° 5' N, long. 62° 4' W. Saw several porpoises about the ship. Gave the people fresh fish for dinner. The pumps were worked an hour in every watch.

Thursday 26th. Little wind from the NE and hazy. People employed in shifting the ballast. At noon lat. 28° 52' N, long. 62° 17' W. Saw a school of flying fish.

Friday 27th. Strong gales from the NNW and a clear sky. People employed in mending the main topsail. At noon lat. 29° 51' N, long. 62° 10' W. Saw Portuguese men-of-war in great numbers. The steward reported the water getting low and put the people on a short allowance.

Saturday 28th. Moderate gales from the N and rainy. People employed in working the pumps. At noon lat. 30° 38' N, long. 63° 57' W. Saw a brig on the larboard bow. The steward reported the water getting low and put the people on a short allowance.

VOYAGE 102. Snow PROVIDENCE, Capt. J. Voss, from Bristol towards Kingston, Jamaica. Sailed Thursday 12 August 1802.

Thursday 12th. Variable winds from the SE and squally. People employed in knotting yarns. At noon lat. 44° 31' N, long. 63° 12' W. Opened a cask of beef, which proved sound. Examined the casks and found three leaking.

VOYAGE 105. Ship HESTER, Capt. N. Pryce, from Cork towards Kingston, Jamaica. Sailed Monday 14 June 1802.

Monday 14th. Steady trades from the N and frequent showers. People employed in setting up the lower rigging. At noon lat. 28° 22' N, long. 13° 28' W.

Tuesday 15th. Variable winds from the W and squally. People employed in bending a new foresail. At noon lat. 27° 32' N, long. 14° 56' W. Saw a sail to windward standing to the eastward. Gave the people fresh fish for dinner. The cook scalded his arm and was laid up two days.

Wednesday 16th. Light airs from the NW and fair weather. People employed in caulking the quarter-deck. At noon lat. 26° 45' N, long. 14° 43' W.

Thursday 5th. Moderate gales from the E and thick fog. People employed in setting up the lower rigging. At noon lat. 33° 59' N, long. 51° 31' W. Saw a floating cask, much weathered. Gave the people fresh fish for dinner. Split the main topgallant sail in a squall; bent another.

VOYAGE 106. Brig MARY ANN, Capt. S. Kemp, from Bristol towards Lisbon. Sailed Sunday 3 October 1802.

Sunday 3rd. Little wind from the SSE and a clear sky. People employed in knotting yarns. At noon lat. 39° 51' N, long. 52° 0' W. Saw a school of flying fish. Heard a noise in the hold and found a cask started; secured it.

VOYAGE 113. Brig MARY ANN, Capt. E. Carew, from Lisbon towards Bristol. Sailed Friday 3 September 1802.

Friday 3rd. Steady trades from the WSW and dark and gloomy. People employed in airing the bedding between decks. At noon lat. 40° 43' N, long. 57° 55' W. Saw several porpoises about the ship. Mustered the people and found all well.

VOYAGE 114. Snow PROVIDENCE, Capt. H. Ainsley, from Bristol towards Kingston, Jamaica. Sailed Monday 1 November 1802.

Monday 1st November. Variable winds from the SW and cloudy. People employed in making points and gaskets. At noon lat. 40° 6' N, long. 58° 50' W. Saw several porpoises about the ship. Split the main topgallant sail in a squall; bent another.

Tuesday 2nd. Moderate gales from the NNW and clear. People employed in setting up the lower rigging. At noon lat. 40° 38' N, long. 60° 2' W. Saw a large turtle asleep on the water.

Saturday 30th. Calms from the SW and a clear sky. People employed in bending a new foresail. At noon lat. 38° 39' N, long. 47° 24' W. Saw a brig on the larboard bow.

Sunday 31st. Gentle breezes from the ESE and dark and gloomy. People employed in shifting the ballast. At noon lat. 37° 29' N, long. 47° 15' W. Saw several porpoises about the ship.

Thursday 4th. Variable winds from the E and hazy. People employed in setting up the lower rigging. At noon lat. 37° 22' N, long. 51° 36' W. Saw Portuguese men-of-war in great numbers. Served the people their allowance of beef and pork. Read the articles of war to the people.

VOYAGE 126. Brig MARY ANN, Capt. S. Kemp, from Bristol towards Kingston, Jamaica. Sailed Sunday 25 July 1802.

Sunday 25th. Little wind from the ESE and hazy. People employed in mending the main topsail. At noon lat. 44° 55' N, long. 53° 47' W. Mustered the people and found all well.

Monday 26th. Variable winds from the W and thick fog. People employed in scraping and tarring the standing rigging. At noon lat. 43° 56' N, long. 54° 53' W. Saw Portuguese men-of-war in great numbers. Read the articles of war to the people.

Tuesday 27th. Gentle breezes from the S and clear. People employed in caulking the quarter-deck. At noon lat. 45° 19' N, long. 56° 3' W. Saw a school of flying fish. The steward reported the water getting low and put the people on a short allowance.

Saturday 3rd. Fresh gales from the NE and squally. People employed in fishing the main yard. At noon lat. 20° 2' N, long. 80° 0' W. Saw Portuguese men-of-war in great numbers. Served the people their allowance of beef and pork. Lost a handspike overboard.

Sunday 4th. Light airs from the SW and rainy. People employed in shifting the ballast. At noon lat. 19° 33' N, long. 80° 0' W. Saw Portuguese men-of-war in great numbers. The cook scalded his arm and was laid up two days.

Monday 5th. Variable winds from the WNW and thick fog. People employed in overhauling the running rigging. At noon lat. 18° 32' N, long. 79° 46' W. Opened a cask of beef, which proved sound.

Tuesday 6th. Strong gales from the ESE and a clear sky. People employed in fishing the main yard. At noon lat. 19° 22' N, long. 80° 0' W. Saw a bird like a gannet.

Wednesday 7th. Little wind from the W and squally. People employed in bending a new foresail. At noon lat. 20° 15' N, long. 80° 0' W. Saw a bird like a gannet. Gave the people fresh fish for dinner.

Thursday 8th. Fresh gales from the SW and clear. People employed in mending the main topsail. At noon lat. 21° 47' N, long. 80° 0' W. Saw a floating cask, much weathered. Heard a noise in the hold and found a cask started; secured it.

Friday 9th. Little wind from the W and fair weather. People employed in setting up the lower rigging. At noon lat. 20° 58' N, long. 80° 0' W. Saw a sail to windward standing to the eastward. The long boat was washed from her chocks and recovered with some damage.

Saturday 10th. Fresh breezes from the WNW and clear. People employed in splicing the cable. At noon lat. 21° 27' N, long. 80° 0' W. Saw Portuguese men-of-war in great numbers. The steward reported the water getting low and put the people on a short allowance.

Sunday 11th. Strong gales from the ENE and a clear sky. People employed in making points and gaskets. At noon lat. 22° 2' N, long. 80° 0' W.

Monday 12th. Strong gales from the ENE and thick fog. People employed in setting up the lower rigging. At noon lat. 20° 54' N, long. 80° 0' W. Saw a ship of war on the starboard tack. Opened a cask of pork, which was found rusty.

Tuesday 13th. Light airs from the NNE and rainy. People employed in shifting the ballast. At noon lat. 22° 2' N, long. 80° 0' W. The long boat was washed from her chocks and recovered with some damage.

Wednesday 14th. Calms from the E and frequent showers. People employed in working the pumps. At noon lat. 21° 46' N, long. 80° 0' W. Opened a cask of beef, which proved sound.

Thursday 15th. Steady trades from the NW and a clear sky. People employed in working the pumps. At noon lat. 22° 55' N, long. 80° 0' W. Opened a cask of beef, which proved sound. The mate had a touch of the ague.

Friday 16th. Variable winds from the ESE and squally. People employed in caulking the quarter-deck. At noon lat. 23° 42' N, long. 80° 0' W.

VOYAGE 133. Brig MARY ANN, Capt. E. Carew, from Kingston, Jamaica towards Bristol. Sailed Thursday 6 May 1802.

Thursday 6th. Steady trades from the NNW and rainy. People employed in bending a new foresail. At noon lat. 30° 44' N, long. 54° 26' W. Served pease and oatmeal.

Friday 7th. Steady trades from the S and thick fog. People employed in shifting the ballast. At noon lat. 30° 1' N, long. 54° 25' W. Saw a brig on the larboard bow. Served bread and cheese to the people.

Saturday 8th. Steady trades from the SSE and clear. People employed in washing and scrubbing the decks. At noon lat. 31° 4' N, long. 56° 12' W. Saw a sail to windward standing to the eastward. Served the people their allowance of beef and pork.

Sunday 9th. Light airs from the ENE and clear. People employed in bending a new foresail. At noon lat. 31° 10' N, long. 56° 4' W. Saw gulf weed in large patches. Served the people their allowance of beef and pork. Split the main topgallant sail in a squall; bent another.

Monday 10th. Steady trades from the W and dark and gloomy. People employed in airing the bedding between decks. At noon lat. 32° 24' N, long. 57° 57' W. The pumps were worked an hour in every watch.

Tuesday 21st. Gentle breezes from the ENE and cloudy. People employed in bending a new foresail. At noon lat. 35° 49' N, long. 31° 30' W. Saw a whale blowing to leeward.

Wednesday 4th. Moderate gales from the ESE and clear. People employed in working the pumps. At noon lat. 29° 56' N, long. 48° 21' W. Saw Portuguese men-of-war in great numbers. Split the main topgallant sail in a squall; bent another.

Thursday 5th. Steady trades from the S and cloudy. People employed in scraping and tarring the standing rigging. At noon lat. 28° 50' N, long. 49° 59' W. Saw a whale blowing to leeward.

Friday 6th. Strong gales from the SSE and fair weather. People employed in stowing the boats. At noon lat. 29° 39' N, long. 51° 5' W. The cook scalded his arm and was laid up two days.

Saturday 7th. Fresh breezes from the W and hazy. People employed in making points and gaskets. At noon lat. 30° 17' N, long. 50° 53' W. Saw Portuguese men-of-war in great numbers. Gave the people fresh fish for dinner.

Sunday 8th. Moderate gales from the ENE and fair weather. People employed in airing the bedding between decks. At noon lat. 31° 48' N, long. 51° 13' W.

Monday 9th. Little wind from the SSE and frequent showers. People employed in setting up the lower rigging. At noon lat. 32° 19' N, long. 52° 3' W. Saw Portuguese men-of-war in great numbers. The long boat was washed from her chocks and recovered with some damage.

Tuesday 10th. Little wind from the NNW and thick fog. People employed in shifting the ballast. At noon lat. 33° 3' N, long. 52° 37' W. Served pease and oatmeal.

Wednesday 11th. Calms from the ESE and cloudy. People employed in washing and scrubbing the decks. At noon lat. 32° 39' N, long. 52° 43' W.

Thursday 12th. Fresh gales from the ENE and rainy. People employed in working the pumps. At noon lat. 33° 35' N, long. 52° 22' W.

Friday 13th. Calms from the ENE and dark and gloomy. People employed in stowing the boats. At noon lat. 34° 52' N, long. 53° 55' W. Saw several porpoises about the ship. Opened a cask of pork, which was found rusty.

Saturday 14th. Calms from the W and squally. People employed in shifting the ballast. At noon lat. 34° 53' N, long. 55° 9' W. Saw Portuguese men-of-war in great numbers. Served pease and oatmeal. The pumps were worked an hour in every watch.

Sunday 15th. Steady trades from the ESE and dark and gloomy. People employed in working the pumps. At noon lat. 35° 44' N, long. 56° 11' W. Saw several porpoises about the ship. Gave the people fresh fish for dinner.

Tuesday 17th. Calms from the SSW and hazy. People employed in splicing the cable. At noon lat. 34° 39' N, long. 58° 35' W. Saw a bird like a gannet. Gave the people fresh fish for dinner. Heard a noise in the hold and found a cask started; secured it.

VOYAGE 138. Brig MARY ANN, Capt. E. Carew, from Bristol towards Kingston, Jamaica. Sailed Friday 19 November 1802.

Friday 19th. Fresh gales from the NW and rainy. People employed in stowing the boats. At noon lat. 31° 47' N, long. 29° 31' W. Saw Portuguese men-of-war in great numbers.

Tuesday 1st June. Variable winds from the NW and hazy. People employed in making points and gaskets. At noon lat. 14° 12' N, long. 51° 53' W. Lost a handspike overboard.

Wednesday 2nd. Fresh breezes from the W and dark and gloomy. People employed in stowing the boats. At noon lat. 14° 9' N, long. 53° 31' W. Saw Portuguese men-of-war in great numbers. Gave the people fresh fish for dinner. The mate had a touch of the ague.

Thursday 3rd. Fresh breezes from the NNW and frequent showers. People employed in setting up the lower rigging. At noon lat. 15° 16' N, long. 55° 3' W.

Friday 4th. Strong gales from the WSW and rainy. People employed in shifting the ballast. At noon lat. 15° 54' N, long. 56° 12' W. Saw a floating cask, much weathered. The pumps were worked an hour in every watch.

Saturday 5th. Light airs from the N and rainy. People employed in bending a new foresail. At noon lat. 14° 45' N, long. 57° 8' W. Saw gulf weed in large patches.

Sunday 6th. Variable winds from the WNW and clear. People employed in making points and gaskets. At noon lat. 14° 35' N, long. 56° 53' W. Lost a handspike overboard.

Monday 7th. Steady trades from the SW and squally. People employed in bending a new foresail. At noon lat. 15° 45' N, long. 58° 35' W. Split the main topgallant sail in a squall; bent another.

Tuesday 8th. Light airs from the NE and rainy. People employed in making points and gaskets. At noon lat. 16° 30' N, long. 59° 32' W. Saw a floating cask, much weathered. Examined the casks and found three leaking.

Wednesday 9th. Moderate gales from the W and clear. People employed in washing and scrubbing the decks. At noon lat. 17° 58' N, long. 61° 8' W. Saw a large turtle asleep on the water. Opened a cask of pork, which was found rusty.

Thursday 10th. Calms from the ESE and squally. People employed in fishing the main yard. At noon lat. 18° 48' N, long. 61° 49' W.

Friday 11th. Fresh breezes from the NNW and squally. People employed in knotting yarns. At noon lat. 18° 4' N, long. 62° 6' W. Gave the people fresh fish for dinner. The cook scalded his arm and was laid up two days.

Saturday 12th. Light airs from the S and fair weather. People employed in stowing the boats. At noon lat. 17° 33' N, long. 63° 45' W. Saw a sail to windward standing to the eastward. Served bread and cheese to the people.

Sunday 13th. Light airs from the N and thick fog. People employed in fishing the main yard. At noon lat. 17° 23' N, long. 63° 49' W. Served a pint of rum to each mess.

Monday 14th. Variable winds from the WSW and fair weather. People employed in mending the main topsail. At noon lat. 18° 37' N, long. 65° 18' W. Saw several porpoises about the ship. Opened a cask of beef, which proved sound. Abel Yeo, seaman, died of a decline, and was buried with the usual ceremony.

VOYAGE 143. Brig MARY ANN, Capt. E. Carew, from Lisbon towards Bristol. Sailed Friday 16 April 1802.

Friday 16th. Variable winds from the E and thick fog. People employed in caulking the quarter-deck. At noon lat. 37° 53' N, long. 50° 41' W. Saw a floating cask, much weathered. Served the people their allowance of beef and pork.

Saturday 17th. Variable winds from the SSW and hazy. People employed in airing the bedding between decks. At noon lat. 39° 6' N, long. 50° 54' W. Saw a ship of war on the starboard tack. Served a pint of rum to each mess.

Sunday 18th. Fresh breezes from the NNE and squally. People employed in airing the bedding between decks. At noon lat. 39° 17' N, long. 51° 40' W. The steward reported the water getting low and put the people on a short allowance.

Monday 19th. Variable winds from the WNW and frequent showers. People employed in making points and gaskets. At noon lat. 39° 16' N, long. 52° 15' W. Saw Portuguese men-of-war in great numbers. Served pease and oatmeal. The cook scalded his arm and was laid up two days.

Tuesday 20th. Little wind from the WSW and thick fog. People employed in mending the main topsail. At noon lat. 39° 12' N, long. 53° 54' W. Opened a cask of pork, which was found rusty. The pumps were worked an hour in every watch.

Thursday 28th. Light airs from the ENE and squally. People employed in washing and scrubbing the decks. At noon lat. 23° 4' N, long. 20° 37' W. Opened a cask of pork, which was found rusty. Lost a handspike overboard.

Friday 29th. Steady trades from the SW and dark and gloomy. People employed in knotting yarns. At noon lat. 24° 4' N, long. 20° 31' W. Saw the loom of land to the southward. Gave the people fresh fish for dinner. The long boat was washed from her chocks and recovered with some damage.

Saturday 30th. Steady trades from the SE and squally. People employed in scraping and tarring the standing rigging. At noon lat. 25° 22' N, long. 20° 43' W. Opened a cask of pork, which was found rusty.

VOYAGE 153. Brig MARY ANN, Capt. E. Carew, from Cork towards Kingston, Jamaica. Sailed Wednesday 21 July 1802.

Wednesday 21st. Variable winds from the WNW and squally. People employed in scraping and tarring the standing rigging. At noon lat. 25° 24' N, long. 64° 4' W. Saw a whale blowing to leeward. Served pease and oatmeal.

Thursday 22nd. Fresh breezes from the NNE and frequent showers. People employed in mending the main topsail. At noon lat. 26° 59' N, long. 65° 12' W. Read the articles of war to the people.

Friday 23rd. Steady trades from the ENE and thick fog. People employed in splicing the cable. At noon lat. 26° 8' N, long. 66° 14' W. Saw a sail to windward standing to the eastward. Served the people their allowance of beef and pork.

Saturday 24th. Gentle breezes from the SSW and rainy. People employed in making points and gaskets. At noon lat. 26° 42' N, long. 66° 29' W. Saw a bird like a gannet.

Sunday 25th. Moderate gales from the NW and cloudy. People employed in fishing the main yard. At noon lat. 27° 16' N, long. 67° 10' W. Saw gulf weed in large patches.

Monday 26th. Variable winds from the ESE and clear. People employed in bending a new foresail. At noon lat. 27° 16' N, long. 66° 50' W. Saw a brig on the larboard bow.

Tuesday 27th. Light airs from the W and thick fog. People employed in scraping and tarring the standing rigging. At noon lat. 28° 14' N, long. 67° 32' W. Saw Portuguese men-of-war in great numbers. Served the people their allowance of beef and pork. The long boat was washed from her chocks and recovered with some damage.

Wednesday 28th. Fresh breezes from the S and rainy. People employed in making points and gaskets. At noon lat. 27° 52' N, long. 67° 48' W. Saw a floating cask, much weathered.

Thursday 29th. Variable winds from the ESE and fair weather. People employed in washing and scrubbing the decks. At noon lat. 27° 47' N, long. 67° 53' W. Saw a ship of war on the starboard tack.

Friday 30th. Fresh gales from the SSW and thick fog. People employed in bending a new foresail. At noon lat. 27° 58' N, long. 69° 32' W. Saw a brig on the larboard bow.

Saturday 31st. Calms from the NE and thick fog. People employed in splicing the cable. At noon lat. 28° 45' N, long. 71° 20' W. Split the main topgallant sail in a squall; bent another.

Sunday 1st August. Strong gales from the SE and thick fog. People employed in washing and scrubbing the decks. At noon lat. 29° 6' N, long. 71° 49' W. Examined the casks and found three leaking.

Monday 2nd. Fresh breezes from the NE and thick fog. People employed in bending a new foresail. At noon lat. 29° 24' N, long. 72° 25' W. Saw Portuguese men-of-war in great numbers.

Tuesday 3rd. Steady trades from the WSW and rainy. People employed in washing and scrubbing the decks. At noon lat. 28° 52' N, long. 73° 18' W. Saw the loom of land to the southward. The cook scalded his arm and was laid up two days.

Wednesday 4th. Little wind from the ESE and dark and gloomy. People employed in mending the main topsail. At noon lat. 29° 21' N, long. 75° 6' W. Examined the casks and found three leaking.

Thursday 5th. Gentle breezes from the WSW and cloudy. People employed in mending the main topsail. At noon lat. 30° 8' N, long. 76° 46' W. Read the articles of war to the people.

Friday 6th. Little wind from the S and cloudy. People employed in mending the main topsail. At noon lat. 29° 24' N, long. 76° 42' W. Served pease and oatmeal.

Saturday 7th. Moderate gales from the WSW and cloudy. People employed in making points and gaskets. At noon lat. 30° 56' N, long. 78° 15' W. Saw a whale blowing to leeward. The pumps were worked an hour in every watch.

Sunday 8th. Calms from the NNE and rainy. People employed in fishing the main yard. At noon lat. 31° 1' N, long. 79° 32' W.

Monday 9th. Variable winds from the E and dark and gloomy. People employed in mending the main topsail. At noon lat. 30° 54' N, long. 80° 0' W. Served bread and cheese to the people.

Tuesday 10th. Calms from the E and a clear sky. People employed in overhauling the running rigging. At noon lat. 31° 28' N, long. 80° 0' W. Served pease and oatmeal.

Wednesday 11th. Calms from the WSW and frequent showers. People employed in airing the bedding between decks. At noon lat. 30° 27' N, long. 80° 0' W. Served bread and cheese to the people. The pumps were worked an hour in every watch.

Thursday 12th. Strong gales from the ENE and a clear sky. People employed in splicing the cable. At noon lat. 30° 35' N, long. 80° 0' W. Saw a large turtle asleep on the water. The mate had a touch of the ague.

Friday 13th. Fresh breezes from the N and clear. People employed in scraping and tarring the standing rigging. At noon lat. 31° 28' N, long. 79° 40' W. Saw a ship of war on the starboard tack. Mustered the people and found all well.

Saturday 14th. Little wind from the S and thick fog. People employed in splicing the cable. At noon lat. 32° 35' N, long. 80° 0' W. Saw a floating cask, much weathered. Served pease and oatmeal. Punished one of the boys for neglect of duty.

Sunday 15th. Calms from the W and frequent showers. People employed in knotting yarns. At noon lat. 31° 37' N, long. 79° 40' W. Served bread and cheese to the people.

Monday 16th. Strong gales from the WSW and frequent showers. People employed in washing and scrubbing the decks. At noon lat. 33° 6' N, long. 80° 0' W. Saw a floating cask, much weathered. Served a pint of rum to each mess.

Tuesday 17th. Fresh gales from the WNW and frequent showers. People employed in airing the bedding between decks. At noon lat. 32° 48' N, long. 79° 50' W. Opened a cask of pork, which was found rusty.

VOYAGE 154. Snow PROVIDENCE, Capt. H. Ainsley, from Bristol towards Lisbon. Sailed Friday 22 October 1802.

Friday 22nd. Fresh gales from the W and frequent showers. People employed in splicing the cable. At noon lat. 15° 47' N, long. 56° 42' W. Saw a sail to windward standing to the eastward. Opened a cask of beef, which proved sound.

Saturday 23rd. Moderate gales from the NNE and squally. People employed in washing and scrubbing the decks. At noon lat. 15° 7' N, long. 58° 17' W. Saw a floating cask, much weathered.

Sunday 2nd. Gentle breezes from the WSW and cloudy. People employed in working the pumps. At noon lat. 39° 19' N, long. 29° 19' W. Saw a bird like a gannet. Examined the casks and found three leaking.

Monday 3rd. Gentle breezes from the W and a clear sky. People employed in washing and scrubbing the decks. At noon lat. 39° 17' N, long. 29° 24' W. Saw a shoal of dolphins.

Tuesday 4th. Little wind from the SSE and a clear sky. People employed in airing the bedding between decks. At noon lat. 39° 5' N, long. 31° 6' W. Saw a ship of war on the starboard tack. Served pease and oatmeal. Examined the casks and found three leaking.

Wednesday 5th. Little wind from the SSW and hazy. People employed in splicing the cable. At noon lat. 38° 59' N, long. 31° 27' W. The mate had a touch of the ague.

Thursday 6th. Fresh gales from the NNW and squally. People employed in making points and gaskets. At noon lat. 39° 25' N, long. 32° 40' W.

Friday 7th. Calms from the ENE and a clear sky. People employed in bending a new foresail. At noon lat. 40° 58' N, long. 32° 35' W. Saw a floating cask, much weathered. Examined the casks and found three leaking.

Saturday 8th. Little wind from the SE and a clear sky. People employed in fishing the main yard. At noon lat. 41° 56' N, long. 33° 22' W.

Sunday 9th. Little wind from the W and frequent showers. People employed in stowing the boats. At noon lat. 40° 44' N, long. 34° 37' W. Saw a bird like a gannet.

Sunday 3rd. Variable winds from the NNE and frequent showers. People employed in fishing the main yard. At noon lat. 32° 39' N, long. 70° 5' W. Gave the people fresh fish for dinner.

Monday 4th. Moderate gales from the NW and cloudy. People employed in stowing the boats. At noon lat. 32° 35' N, long. 70° 3' W. Saw the loom of land to the southward. Served a pint of rum to each mess.

Tuesday 5th. Fresh gales from the SSE and clear. People employed in scraping and tarring the standing rigging. At noon lat. 33° 9' N, long. 71° 6' W.

Wednesday 6th. Calms from the N and clear. People employed in scraping and tarring the standing rigging. At noon lat. 32° 1' N, long. 72° 28' W. Saw a shoal of dolphins. Served pease and oatmeal. Mustered the people and found all well.

Thursday 7th. Fresh gales from the ESE and a clear sky. People employed in mending the main topsail. At noon lat. 33° 19' N, long. 73° 47' W. Saw Portuguese men-of-war in great numbers. Opened a cask of beef, which proved sound. Mustered the people and found all well.

Friday 8th. Strong gales from the NNW and fair weather. People employed in splicing the cable. At noon lat. 32° 51' N, long. 75° 0' W. Saw a ship of war on the starboard tack. The steward reported the water getting low and put the people on a short allowance.

Saturday 9th. Fresh breezes from the ESE and a clear sky. People employed in setting up the lower rigging. At noon lat. 32° 30' N, long. 75° 5' W. Saw a shoal of dolphins. Served the people their allowance of beef and pork. Examined the casks and found three leaking.

Sunday 10th. Strong gales from the WSW and squally. People employed in airing the bedding between decks. At noon lat. 33° 51' N, long. 75° 30' W. Saw a shoal of dolphins.

Monday 11th. Fresh gales from the NW and hazy. People employed in knotting yarns. At noon lat. 32° 41' N, long. 76° 48' W. The mate had a touch of the ague.

Tuesday 12th. Gentle breezes from the ENE and clear. People employed in bending a new foresail. At noon lat. 31° 40' N, long. 76° 33' W. Saw a ship of war on the starboard tack. Served pease and oatmeal. The mate had a touch of the ague.

Wednesday 13th. Calms from the SSE and clear. People employed in fishing the main yard. At noon lat. 32° 46' N, long. 76° 23' W. Saw several porpoises about the ship.

Thursday 14th. Strong gales from the S and rainy. People employed in washing and scrubbing the decks. At noon lat. 32° 31' N, long. 77° 21' W. Saw a floating cask, much weathered. Served pease and oatmeal.

Friday 15th. Steady trades from the SSW and clear. People employed in setting up the lower rigging. At noon lat. 33° 24' N, long. 78° 6' W. Split the main topgallant sail in a squall; bent another.

VOYAGE 165. Ship HESTER, Capt. N. Pryce, from Cork towards Kingston, Jamaica. Sailed Monday 22 November 1802.

Monday 22nd. Light airs from the NNW and frequent showers. People employed in overhauling the running rigging. At noon lat. 20° 35' N, long. 29° 56' W. Saw a brig on the larboard bow. Served the people their allowance of beef and pork.

Tuesday 23rd. Fresh breezes from the SW and cloudy. People employed in stowing the boats. At noon lat. 21° 2' N, long. 29° 51' W. Saw a brig on the larboard bow. Opened a cask of beef, which proved sound.

Wednesday 24th. Little wind from the ENE and squally. People employed in shifting the ballast. At noon lat. 21° 54' N, long. 31° 32' W. Saw a sail to windward standing to the eastward. Gave the people fresh fish for dinner.

Thursday 25th. Little wind from the SW and thick fog. People employed in airing the bedding between decks. At noon lat. 22° 6' N, long. 32° 47' W. Gave the people fresh fish for dinner.

Friday 26th. Moderate gales from the S and squally. People employed in knotting yarns. At noon lat. 23° 39' N, long. 34° 2' W. Saw a ship of war on the starboard tack. Mustered the people and found all well.

Saturday 27th. Strong gales from the NNE and frequent showers. People employed in knotting yarns. At noon lat. 23° 10' N, long. 34° 55' W. Opened a cask of beef, which proved sound. Daniel Cole, seaman, died of a decline, and was buried with the usual ceremony.

Sunday 28th. Gentle breezes from the SE and rainy. People employed in caulking the quarter-deck. At noon lat. 23° 36' N, long. 36° 33' W. Saw several porpoises about the ship. Served a pint of rum to each mess.

Monday 29th. Moderate gales from the ENE and thick fog. People employed in bending a new foresail. At noon lat. 22° 49' N, long. 38° 3' W. Saw several porpoises about the ship. Served a pint of rum to each mess.

Tuesday 30th. Fresh breezes from the NNE and dark and gloomy. People employed in working the pumps. At noon lat. 22° 16' N, long. 38° 51' W. Saw gulf weed in large patches.

Wednesday 12th. Variable winds from the W and frequent showers. People employed in overhauling the running rigging. At noon lat. 27° 36' N, long. 61° 17' W. Saw the loom of land to the southward. Served bread and cheese to the people.

Thursday 13th. Light airs from the NW and dark and gloomy. People employed in airing the bedding between decks. At noon lat. 26° 35' N, long. 63° 8' W. Punished one of the boys for neglect of duty.

Friday 14th. Fresh breezes from the WNW and fair weather. People employed in working the pumps. At noon lat. 26° 39' N, long. 63° 38' W. Saw a sail to windward standing to the eastward. Served pease and oatmeal. The mate had a touch of the ague.

Saturday 15th. Calms from the ESE and thick fog. People employed in caulking the quarter-deck. At noon lat. 25° 35' N, long. 65° 16' W. Saw a whale blowing to leeward. Opened a cask of beef, which proved sound.

Sunday 16th. Variable winds from the ENE and clear. People employed in setting up the lower rigging. At noon lat. 24° 51' N, long. 65° 20' W. Saw a whale blowing to leeward. Opened a cask of pork, which was found rusty. George Cole, seaman, died of a fever, and was buried with the usual ceremony.

Monday 17th. Light airs from the WNW and thick fog. People employed in airing the bedding between decks. At noon lat. 24° 16' N, long. 66° 24' W. Saw a school of flying fish. Opened a cask of pork, which was found rusty. Examined the casks and found three leaking.

VOYAGE 176. Brig MARY ANN, Capt. S. Kemp, from Bristol towards Cork. Sailed Sunday 23 May 1802.

Sunday 23rd. Steady trades from the ESE and squally. People employed in setting up the lower rigging. At noon lat. 36° 44' N, long. 16° 15' W. Saw Portuguese men-of-war in great numbers. Served the people their allowance of beef and pork. The pumps were worked an hour in every watch.

Monday 24th. Fresh gales from the SSW and dark and gloomy. People employed in bending a new foresail. At noon lat. 36° 9' N, long. 18° 2' W. Saw several porpoises about the ship. Mustered the people and found all well.

VOYAGE 182. Snow PROVIDENCE, Capt. J. Voss, from Bristol towards Cork. Sailed Thursday 23 September 1802.

Thursday 23rd. Variable winds from the WSW and hazy. People employed in mending the main topsail. At noon lat. 45° 44' N, long. 59° 54' W. Saw a shoal of dolphins.

Monday 26th. Fresh gales from the S and thick fog. People employed in airing the bedding between decks. At noon lat. 14° 31' N, long. 77° 28' W. Saw a ship of war on the starboard tack. Wednesday 3rd. Little wind from the NW and a clear sky. People employed in setting up the lower rigging. At noon lat. 47° 30' N, long. 72° 17' W. Saw a whale blowing to leeward.

Thursday 4th. Fresh breezes from the SSE and dark and gloomy. People employed in setting up the lower rigging. At noon lat. 46° 45' N, long. 73° 51' W. Saw a large turtle asleep on the water. Served bread and cheese to the people.

Friday 5th. Fresh breezes from the ESE and rainy. People employed in washing and scrubbing the decks. At noon lat. 48° 18' N, long. 74° 52' W. Saw a school of flying fish.

Saturday 6th. Fresh gales from the SW and thick fog. People employed in caulking the quarter-deck. At noon lat. 49° 50' N, long. 76° 14' W. Saw a shoal of dolphins. Served the people their allowance of beef and pork.

Sunday 7th. Light airs from the E and squally. People employed in airing the bedding between decks. At noon lat. 50° 25' N, long. 77° 32' W. Saw a sail to windward standing to the eastward.

Monday 8th. Light airs from the E and dark and gloomy. People employed in washing and scrubbing the decks. At noon lat. 51° 3' N, long. 79° 7' W. Saw a ship of war on the starboard tack.

Tuesday 9th. Fresh gales from the NNE and cloudy. People employed in caulking the quarter-deck. At noon lat. 51° 25' N, long. 79° 44' W. Saw a floating cask, much weathered. Examined the casks and found three leaking.

Wednesday 10th. Light airs from the N and rainy. People employed in making points and gaskets. At noon lat. 52° 39' N, long. 80° 0' W. Saw the loom of land to the southward. Gave the people fresh fish for dinner.

VOYAGE 187. Snow PROVIDENCE, Capt. J. Voss, from Kingston, Jamaica towards Bristol. Sailed Monday 22 November 1802.

Monday 22nd. Fresh breezes from the E and cloudy. People employed in knotting yarns. At noon lat. 43° 24' N, long. 26° 20' W. Saw a shoal of dolphins. Gave the people fresh fish for dinner. The cook scalded his arm and was laid up two days.

Thursday 27th. Little wind from the W and cloudy. People employed in working the pumps. At noon lat. 18° 8' N, long. 61° 55' W. Saw a ship of war on the starboard tack. Gave the people fresh fish for dinner. The long boat was washed from her chocks and recovered with some damage.

Wednesday 22nd. Gentle breezes from the E and thick fog. People employed in shifting the ballast. At noon lat. 47° 41' N, long. 17° 42' W. Saw a whale blowing to leeward. The mate had a touch of the ague.

Monday 1st March. Little wind from the NW and a clear sky. People employed in setting up the lower rigging. At noon lat. 19° 18' N, long. 69° 26' W. Saw a whale blowing to leeward. Split the main topgallant sail in a squall; bent another.

Tuesday 2nd. Strong gales from the SSE and frequent showers. People employed in bending a new foresail. At noon lat. 20° 16' N, long. 69° 22' W. Served a pint of rum to each mess. Punished one of the boys for neglect of duty.

Wednesday 3rd. Fresh gales from the E and hazy. People employed in stowing the boats. At noon lat. 21° 39' N, long. 69° 38' W. Peter Nash, seaman, died of the flux, and was buried with the usual ceremony.

Thursday 4th. Steady trades from the NNE and a clear sky. People employed in caulking the quarter-deck. At noon lat. 22° 17' N, long. 69° 29' W. The mate had a touch of the ague.

VOYAGE 193. Brig MARY ANN, Capt. E. Carew, from Kingston, Jamaica towards Bristol. Sailed Thursday 6 May 1802.

Thursday 6th. Variable winds from the NE and cloudy. People employed in splicing the cable. At noon lat. 33° 56' N, long. 7° 17' W.

Friday 1st January. Fresh gales from the E and dark and gloomy. People employed in setting up the lower rigging. At noon lat. 20° 44' N, long. 46° 47' W. Saw a large turtle asleep on the water. Opened a cask of pork, which was found rusty.

Saturday 2nd. Light airs from the NE and fair weather. People employed in washing and scrubbing the decks. At noon lat. 21° 46' N, long. 47° 52' W. Saw several porpoises about the ship. Served bread and cheese to the people.

Sunday 3rd. Moderate gales from the SSE and rainy. People employed in working the pumps. At noon lat. 23° 18' N, long. 48° 40' W. Saw a brig on the larboard bow. Opened a cask of beef, which proved sound. Examined the casks and found three leaking.

Monday 4th. Gentle breezes from the NNE and a clear sky. People employed in setting up the lower rigging. At noon lat. 23° 29' N, long. 49° 2' W. Saw a school of flying fish. Read the articles of war to the people.

Tuesday 5th. Light airs from the NW and squally. People employed in setting up the lower rigging. At noon lat. 22° 36' N, long. 50° 34' W. Saw a sail to windward standing to the eastward. Served the people their allowance of beef and pork.

Wednesday 6th. Moderate gales from the SSW and rainy. People employed in bending a new foresail. At noon lat. 22° 10' N, long. 51° 9' W. Saw a brig on the larboard bow.

Thursday 7th. Steady trades from the NNE and rainy. People employed in overhauling the running rigging. At noon lat. 22° 39' N, long. 51° 17' W. Served a pint of rum to each mess.

Friday 8th. Fresh breezes from the WSW and cloudy. People employed in fishing the main yard. At noon lat. 23° 23' N, long. 53° 1' W. Saw a floating cask, much weathered.

Saturday 9th. Calms from the S and frequent showers. People employed in airing the bedding between decks. At noon lat. 22° 13' N, long. 54° 44' W. Saw several porpoises about the ship. Opened a cask of beef, which proved sound.

Sunday 10th. Strong gales from the NE and dark and gloomy. People employed in stowing the boats. At noon lat. 23° 46' N, long. 56° 36' W. Opened a cask of beef, which proved sound. The steward reported the water getting low and put the people on a short allowance.

Monday 11th. Moderate gales from the N and a clear sky. People employed in knotting yarns. At noon lat. 23° 51' N, long. 57° 21' W. Served a pint of rum to each mess. The mate had a touch of the ague.

Tuesday 12th. Fresh gales from the NNE and dark and gloomy. People employed in knotting yarns. At noon lat. 25° 19' N, long. 56° 58' W. Saw Portuguese men-of-war in great numbers. Served the people their allowance of beef and pork. Split the main topgallant sail in a squall; bent another.

Monday 10th. Strong gales from the W and a clear sky. People employed in overhauling the running rigging. At noon lat. 46° 45' N, long. 75° 47' W. Gave the people fresh fish for dinner.

VOYAGE 201. Brig MARY ANN, Capt. S. Kemp, from Cork towards Kingston, Jamaica. Sailed Wednesday 21 July 1802.

Wednesday 21st. Little wind from the ESE and thick fog. People employed in setting up the lower rigging. At noon lat. 31° 15' N, long. 57° 8' W.

Thursday 22nd. Variable winds from the NNE and a clear sky. People employed in splicing the cable. At noon lat. 32° 32' N, long. 58° 12' W. Examined the casks and found three leaking.

Friday 23rd. Gentle breezes from the N and clear. People employed in stowing the boats. At noon lat. 33° 30' N, long. 57° 51' W. Saw the loom of land to the southward. Gave the people fresh fish for dinner. Mustered the people and found all well.

VOYAGE 206. Brig MARY ANN, Capt. S. Kemp, from Bristol towards Cork. Sailed Friday 15 October 1802.

Friday 15th. Variable winds from the NE and cloudy. People employed in washing and scrubbing the decks. At noon lat. 45° 34' N, long. 8° 42' W. Saw a ship of war on the starboard tack. Served the people their allowance of beef and pork.

Saturday 16th. Moderate gales from the ENE and cloudy. People employed in knotting yarns. At noon lat. 45° 15' N, long. 9° 25' W. Saw a floating cask, much weathered.

Sunday 17th. Steady trades from the NE and fair weather. People employed in mending the main topsail. At noon lat. 44° 51' N, long. 9° 20' W. Saw several porpoises about the ship. Peter Dodd, seaman, died of a decline, and was buried with the usual ceremony.

Monday 18th. Fresh gales from the W and cloudy. People employed in stowing the boats. At noon lat. 45° 54' N, long. 11° 11' W. Saw the loom of land to the southward.

Tuesday 19th. Fresh gales from the ESE and dark and gloomy. People employed in overhauling the running rigging. At noon lat. 46° 21' N, long. 12° 27' W.

Wednesday 20th. Steady trades from the NNW and cloudy. People employed in fishing the main yard. At noon lat. 45° 16' N, long. 12° 29' W. Saw Portuguese men-of-war in great numbers. Read the articles of war to the people.

Thursday 21st. Little wind from the S and thick fog. People employed in overhauling the running rigging. At noon lat. 44° 26' N, long. 12° 36' W. Saw a shoal of dolphins. Mustered the people and found all well.

Friday 22nd. Steady trades from the NE and fair weather. People employed in mending the main topsail. At noon lat. 43° 56' N, long. 13° 50' W. Served pease and oatmeal.

Saturday 23rd. Little wind from the SW and fair weather. People employed in shifting the ballast. At noon lat. 43° 48' N, long. 13° 42' W. Served a pint of rum to each mess.

Sunday 24th. Strong gales from the W and a clear sky. People employed in knotting yarns. At noon lat. 45° 22' N, long. 15° 27' W.

Monday 25th. Gentle breezes from the SSW and squally. People employed in shifting the ballast. At noon lat. 46° 13' N, long. 15° 50' W. Saw a large turtle asleep on the water. Served the people their allowance of beef and pork.

Tuesday 26th. Little wind from the NNW and fair weather. People employed in knotting yarns. At noon lat. 46° 25' N, long. 16° 59' W. Saw a large turtle asleep on the water. Lost a handspike overboard.

Friday 29th. Fresh gales from the SW and squally. People employed in airing the bedding between decks. At noon lat. 48° 12' N, long. 16° 56' W. Gave the people fresh fish for dinner. Heard a noise in the hold and found a cask started; secured it.

Saturday 30th. Fresh breezes from the NNE and a clear sky. People employed in mending the main topsail. At noon lat. 47° 24' N, long. 18° 28' W. Saw a bird like a gannet.

Sunday 31st. Little wind from the S and thick fog. People employed in fishing the main yard. At noon lat. 46° 39' N, long. 19° 21' W. Served bread and cheese to the people. The steward reported the water getting low and put the people on a short allowance. Nathaniel Yates, seaman, was lost overboard in the night, and was buried with the usual ceremony.
